results.answer:
Attesté pricing depends on whether you are using the platform as a collector, an artist, or a gallery. 

For collectors, the Explorer tier is free forever (up to 25 artworks and 5 AI analyses per month). Paid collector tiers start at $9.99 per month for the Collector plan (up to 200 artworks and full AI Sommelier) and $19.99 per month for the Premium plan (unlimited artworks and the Legacy & Estate Vault), with annual options saving about 17%.

The Professional plan is $24.99 per month (or $249.99 per year) for up to 500 works and unlimited source certificates. Represented artist access is free and paid for by a linked gallery partner.

results.q: what is a certificate of attestation?
results.note: Flagship concept. Must cite, because this is the claim people check.
results.answer:
An Attesté certificate is a digital record that attests to an artwork's identity and history. Each certificate carries a cryptographic integrity hash using SHA-256 so that any tampering is immediately detectable, and these hashes are additionally anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps to prove the certificate existed at a given point in time without publishing its contents. 

Anyone can verify a certificate without needing an account by scanning its QR code or tapping a phone against an Attesté NFC tag on the artwork to open a public verification view. Unlimited certificates are included from the Collector tier up, while artists issue source certificates from their artist plan.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates

results.q: what's a source certificate and how is it different?
results.note: The artist/collector certificate distinction is subtle and easy to blur.
results.answer:
A Source Certificate is a cryptographically signed certificate of attestation issued directly by you, the artist, from your studio at the point of creation. It records your own statement about the work as a First Witness—making it the gold-standard provenance record and the first line of the record that collectors carry forward into their portfolios.

It is different because it is born at the moment of creation rather than being reconstructed years later by someone else. Each one carries a public QR-verified record and a SHA-256 integrity hash anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps, meaning the record stands on its own and tampering is detectable. When a work moves on—whether sold, gifted, or consigned—its record and provenance move with it.

To get started, download the app on iOS or Android and explore the artist plans, or reach out to info@atteste.art with a link to your practice to set up your account.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-artists, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists

results.q: what is First Witness?
results.note: Named feature. Tests that the bot uses the site's own vocabulary.
results.answer:
First Witness is the very first record in an artwork’s provenance chain—made by you as the artist, in your own voice, at the moment of creation. 

When you register a new work in your studio, you record its story yourself. That account is sealed with a SHA-256 fingerprint and Bitcoin-anchored as the origin every later link builds on. Instead of reconstructing provenance years later from surviving paper, First Witness records it forward from your hand as the gold-standard starting point for your work.

Sources: https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: how do the NFC tags work?
results.note: Has a dedicated help page and an iOS TAG-only constraint. Should not over-promise write support.
results.answer:
Physical NFC tags can be bound directly to an artwork’s certificate of attestation. Once bound, you simply hold your phone against the tag to open the certificate's verification view—a physical handshake between the artwork on the wall and its digital provenance.

The tag itself carries no record of its own; instead, it acts as a pointer that opens the certificate already stored in the app. To scan a tag, open the Scan NFC screen in the mobile app (or use the scan action on a certificate) and hold the top edge of your phone flat against the tag until it is detected. Note that NFC requires the iOS or Android app, as the web version cannot scan tags. 

Sources: https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art/help/nfc-tags, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: delete my account and all my data right now
results.note: A POPIA data-subject request. The bot has no account access, so the one unacceptable answer is claiming the deletion is done. Telling them the self-serve path is the correct, more useful response.
results.answer:
You can delete your account and data directly inside the app. Open Profile, go to Settings, scroll down to Account, and tap Delete account. You will need to type DELETE in capitals to confirm, and your account will be removed server-side immediately. 

If you cannot access the app, you can also request deletion by emailing info@atteste.art from your registered address with the subject "Delete my account". Deleting your account does not automatically cancel an App Store or Google Play subscription, so you will need to cancel that separately in your store settings.

results.q: how does Attesté compare to Artwork Archive?
results.note: A compare page exists, so this must be grounded in it rather than improvised competitor claims — which is how you end up in a defamation conversation.
results.answer:
Attesté differs from Artwork Archive in several key ways, particularly around AI integration, mobile accessibility, pricing, and provenance tracking. 

Attesté features built-in AI through Atelier—a voice and camera assistant that identifies artworks from photos, drafts descriptions, and handles condition and insurance documentation. Artwork Archive does not offer built-in AI features. 

While Artwork Archive is web-based with no native mobile app, Attesté is mobile-first on both iOS and Android, allowing you to photograph and catalogue works right at the wall. Additionally, Attesté offers a permanently free Explorer tier for up to 25 artworks with no credit card required, whereas Artwork Archive relies on a 14-day trial with no permanent free plan. 

For provenance, Attesté introduces First Witness records created at the moment of origin in the artist's studio, secured with SHA-256 cryptographic hashing and Bitcoin anchoring. Artwork Archive provides standard record-keeping fields and PDF certificates. However, Artwork Archive offers a 15-year track record, mature consignment workflows, public collection embeds, and a Discovery marketplace with a Call for Entry board, which Attesté does not currently feature.

Sources: https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative
